Three refusals, no flag turns them off: POSITIONAL (a bare stamp on the opening line or a subscript reading-time line), MIXED (the token plus a bare stamp elsewhere — the case the card names), UNKNOWN (a token surviving substitution, so a mistyped a mistyped NOW token cannot post literally and leave the artefact unstamped). The positional one is NOT the mixed one widened: mixed alone never fires on a seat that simply never types the token, which is every comment in the recorded failure. Then it reads the artefact back and prints id, url, the platform's own write time, the drift against it, and a byte comparison of the stored body — proof, not assumption. READ SIDE: H56 in check-half-states.mjs, report-only, band state (H44's band — H44's class one field over: a reading that cannot be dated, and one whose date is wrong). It reads exactly H44's corpus and buys no request, placed after H44's loop and before H46 so the two censuses describe one population. Two false-positive sources closed: a minute-grained stamp is widened to its own minute (otherwise every correctly stamped comment files a row), and an edited comment is judged against the whole created_at..updated_at window. A line with more than one stamp is HELD OUT and counted, never guessed at, so rows are a lower bound and the census says by how much. The two sides import ONE stamp definition, ONE position reader and ONE tolerance from check-half-states.mjs, so they cannot come to disagree.
